evals.prompt: Review PR 2481 in elastic/docs-content. It adds a new page at deploy-manage/autoscaling/ece-autoscaling-limits.md, updates the parent overview page to link to it, and adds an entry to the navigation file.
evals.expected_output: Confirms the PR head ref is checked out, reads both changed pages in full, dispatches the companion review skills, and produces one report sectioned by the six review criteria with a recommended approve, comment, or request-changes call.
expectations: Loads the rubric from references/review-criteria.md, and refreshes it from the elastic-internal-docs MCP or states in the report header that the MCP was not reachable
Dispatches docs-content-type-checker and docs-check-contradictions, and reports which dispatch path was used for each
Report contains all six criteria sections: user focus, technical accuracy, applicability, maintainability, language, style
Checks whether the new page is cross-referenced from its parent page so users are not stranded
Ends with an explicit Approve / Comment / Request changes recommendation with reasoning
Does NOT edit any file, post a GitHub comment, or run gh pr review

evals.prompt: Review the current branch. It changes applies_to tags on two existing pages in solutions/observability/ to add serverless availability. No code samples or images are touched.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the branch diff against its base, dispatches docs-applies-to-tagging because applies_to changed, skips docs-validate-code-samples because no code blocks changed, and reports against the full checklist.
expectations: Dispatches docs-applies-to-tagging
Does NOT dispatch docs-validate-code-samples, and states in the companion run table that it was skipped as not relevant
Still reports on all six criteria rather than only applicability
Checks backport labels when PR metadata is available, or states that PR-only checks were skipped for a branch or path input
Dispatches docs-applies-to-tagging through a subagent rather than the Skill tool, because it declares Edit
No applies_to tag is written into any file; git status is unchanged after the review
Waits for every dispatched companion to return before writing the report, and does NOT invent findings for one still pending

Resolves the branch base from the PR's baseRefName or the repository default branch, and does NOT use the upstream tracking branch (@{u}), which is the branch's own remote copy and yields an empty diff

evals.prompt: Review PR 3102 in elastic/docs-content. It is a small, well-written change: it corrects a default timeout value on one how-to page, the applies_to tags are already correct, the wording follows the style guide, and the PR body links to the engineering issue confirming the new value.
evals.expected_output: Runs the full checklist, finds nothing blocking, notes the SME evidence in the PR body, and recommends Approve without manufacturing findings.
expectations: Recommends Approve
Marks criteria that were checked and came back clean as Clean, distinct from Not checked
Does NOT manufacture low-value findings to appear thorough
Does NOT report unrelated pre-existing issues as blockers; any such observation appears in a separate pre-existing section
Notes that the linked engineering issue provides the authoritative source for the changed value

evals.prompt: Review PR 2903 in elastic/docs-content. It deletes deploy-manage/monitoring/stack-monitoring-legacy.md and folds the content into deploy-manage/monitoring/stack-monitoring.md. The diff does not touch redirects.yml.
evals.expected_output: Flags the missing redirect as a high-severity maintainability finding, checks whether images or snippets from the deleted page are now orphaned or still referenced, and recommends Request changes.
expectations: Flags the missing redirect entry for the deleted page at High severity under Maintainability, after checking both redirects.yml and _redirects.yml next to the content set's docset.yml
Greps the repository for remaining references to the deleted page path
Checks whether images or snippets used only by the deleted page are now unused
Recommends Request changes, because broken incoming links prevent users from reaching the content
Reads the deleted page from the base ref (git show), since it is absent from the checked-out head
Initializes BASE and BASE_REPO during PR target resolution, so the base fetch for the deleted page does not run with empty values

evals.prompt: Review PR 2481 in elastic/docs-content. (The working tree is currently on the main branch, not the PR head ref, and has no uncommitted changes.)
evals.expected_output: Detects that the checked-out ref does not match the PR head ref, surfaces the mismatch, and asks before running gh pr checkout rather than silently reviewing the base tree.
expectations: Detects and reports the mismatch between the PR head ref and the checked-out branch
Asks the user before running gh pr checkout, and does NOT check out the branch without confirmation
If the user declines, marks repository hygiene checks as Not checked because they ran against a different ref
Does NOT report orphaned-image or missing-redirect checks as clean while on the wrong ref
Treats only tracked modifications as blocking; an untracked file such as a scratch directory does not prevent offering gh pr checkout

evals.prompt: Review PR 2755 in elastic/docs-content. (Only docs-check-style and content-type-checker are installed; check-contradictions, frontmatter-audit, and flag-jargon-skill are not installed on this machine, and the elastic-internal-docs MCP is not reachable.)
evals.expected_output: Loads the rubric from references/review-criteria.md, reports the criteria whose companions are missing as Not checked with the install command, and does not present unchecked criteria as clean.
expectations: Reads references/review-criteria.md and states in the report header that the rubric was not refreshed because the MCP is unreachable
Marks the criteria backed by the uninstalled companions as Not checked, naming each missing skill
Gives the install command using the companion's frontmatter name, for example 'docs-check-contradictions', matching the form documented in README.md
Does NOT substitute its own judgment for a companion that did not run, and does NOT mark those criteria Clean
Still completes the orchestrator-only checks in Step 4 and produces a recommended action

evals.prompt: Review the current branch. It is a pushed feature branch with three changed docs pages, and it tracks its own remote copy at origin/<branch-name>.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the base to the repository's default branch or the PR's base, not the upstream tracking branch, finds the three changed files, and reviews them.
expectations: Resolves the base via gh pr view baseRefName or the repository default branch
Does NOT use git rev-parse --abbrev-ref @{u} or the upstream tracking branch as the diff base
Finds the three changed files rather than reporting an empty diff
If the diff does come back empty, stops and reports a base-resolution problem instead of reporting a clean review
Captures line ranges, not only changed paths, so findings can be scoped in Step 5
Fetches the base branch from the base repository rather than assuming origin/<base> is correct
Detects that the branch has an open PR via gh pr view with no number, and runs the PR-only checks (labels, author, PR body) rather than reporting them skipped

evals.prompt: Review PR 4120 in elastic/docs-content. It was opened from a contributor's fork (isCrossRepository is true) and changes two pages. The working directory is a clone of elastic/docs-content, currently on main.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the fork PR as reviewable from the base-repo clone, offers gh pr checkout, and does not reject the repository as unrelated.
expectations: Does NOT reject the repository as wrong or unrelated because headRepository is the contributor's fork
Compares the local repository against the PR's base repository, not headRepository
Detects the ref mismatch and offers gh pr checkout, which fetches the fork's head into a local branch
Fetches the base branch from the base repository, not from origin, when reading base versions of deleted files
Completes the review rather than stopping at target resolution

evals.prompt: Review PR 8290 in elastic/docs-content. It recalibrates create-serverless-project.md into step-by-step instructions and moves the project-type cards to serverless.md. The page's frontmatter has no type field. The intro opens with 'There are a few options...' and prerequisites are scattered through intro bullets.
evals.expected_output: Reports the how-to structural findings, recommends adding type: how-to to the frontmatter, and cites the governing style guide page or section on each language and style finding.
expectations: Recommends adding `type: how-to` to the page's frontmatter, naming the content type
Makes that recommendation even though the page is an edit to an existing page rather than a new page from a template
Every Language and Style finding carries a Guideline link to the style guide page or section that decides it
Uses section anchors where they exist, for example voice-tone#active-and-passive-voice or seo#headings, rather than linking only the top-level style guide
Does NOT invent an anchor; when no listed link covers a finding, cites the page and says which part applies
Passes through a companion's own rule name, such as a Vale rule like Elastic.OxfordComma, alongside the guideline link

evals.prompt: Review PR 9001 in elastic/docs-content. The PR body says 'Docs for elastic/elasticsearch#141516'. That code PR renames the setting indices.recovery.max_bytes_per_sec, changes its default from 40mb to 80mb, and landed on branch 8.19. The docs page is tagged applies_to stack: ga 9.2 and still documents the old default.
evals.expected_output: Reads the linked code PR and its diff, flags the stale default and the version mismatch between the code PR's base branch and the page's applies_to, and cites the code PR for each finding.
expectations: Resolves and reads the linked elasticsearch PR using gh pr view/diff with --repo or a full URL, not the owner/repo#number shorthand, rather than only noting that a link exists
Flags that the documented default no longer matches the value in the code diff
Flags the mismatch between the code PR's base branch (8.19) and the page's applies_to (9.2)
Cites the linked code PR and the file in its diff so the writer can follow the same trail
Does NOT claim the docs change is technically correct merely because parts of it matched the diff
Does NOT flag documented claims that are simply absent from the code diff as errors

evals.prompt: Review PR 9100 in elastic/docs-content. It clarifies wording on an existing concept page. The PR body links no code PR, issue, or commit, and no engineering repository is referenced anywhere.
evals.expected_output: Reports that no authoritative source is cited, and does not go looking for a code change to verify against.
expectations: Reports under Technical accuracy that no SME sign-off or authoritative source is cited
Does NOT search repositories or attempt source verification when no code change is referenced
Does NOT fabricate a linked code PR or speculate about which repository the change relates to
Completes the other five criteria normally

evals.prompt: Review PR 8290 in elastic/docs-content. All seven companion skills are installed. During the run, docs-check-style is dispatched but never returns.
evals.expected_output: Dispatches all five Always-gated companions separately, reports docs-check-style as did not return, and does not author Language or Style findings in its place.
expectations: Dispatches docs-check-style, docs-flag-jargon-skill, docs-content-type-checker, docs-check-contradictions and docs-frontmatter-audit as five separate calls, never bundled into combined agents
The companion run table has exactly seven rows and no Always-gated companion is marked Not dispatched
Marks docs-check-style as Not checked — companion did not return
Does NOT substitute its own style assessment for the missing companion, and does NOT label the gap manual assessment
Any finding it made itself under Step 4 is sourced docs-review-pr and kept separate from the missing companion's slot
Uses one consistent table format across all six sections, with Clean and Not checked as section-level statuses rather than Severity values
